title: St. Augustine
name: St. Augustine
metaTitle: St. Augustine 1031 Exchange Services | 1031 Exchange Jacksonville
metaDescription: St. Augustine 1031 exchange scope covering historic-district retail, King Street and San Marco Avenue storefronts, and St. Johns County review requirements.

sections.html: St. Augustine sits in St. Johns County, a separate taxing and permitting jurisdiction from Duval County, and its identification package looks nothing like a submittal written for downtown Jacksonville. The city's historic core runs its own design-review process, and a scope narrative that ignores that fact will stall at the first submission.

sections.heading: A Historic District With Its Own Approval Track
sections.html:
Commercial buildings along King Street, St. George Street, and San Marco Avenue fall inside the city's Historic Preservation review boundaries, and any exterior change, signage swap, or facade update on these parcels requires a Certificate of Appropriateness before a contractor can pull a permit. A buyer coming from a suburban net-lease background should budget extra weeks into the closing schedule specifically for this review, since it runs on a separate calendar from standard building-permit processing.

Floor plates in the historic core also tend to be narrow and deep, a legacy of the city's colonial-era lot lines, which limits what tenant mix a given storefront can realistically support without a costly interior reconfiguration.

Structural condition on these buildings varies widely by construction era, and a scope-of-condition report should distinguish coquina-and-masonry construction dating to the Spanish colonial and territorial periods from wood-frame commercial buildings added later in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, since each carries a different renovation cost profile and a different set of preservation-board expectations for any repair work.

sections.heading: What Actually Trades in This Submarket
sections.html:
The identification candidates that come up most often on a St. Augustine scope of work are:

  • historic storefront retail along King Street and St. George Street
  • tourism-driven restaurant and hospitality buildings near the bayfront
  • small mixed-use buildings with ground-floor retail and upper-floor office
  • bed-and-breakfast and boutique lodging conversions in residential-adjacent zones
  • newer commercial pads along US-1 and State Road 16 outside the historic boundary

sections.heading: Tourism as a Demand Driver, and Its Seasonality
sections.html: St. Augustine's visitor economy is the primary driver behind restaurant and retail rents in the historic core, and that demand carries a seasonal pattern tied to weather and the school calendar rather than the steadier, year-round pattern typical of a suburban net-lease pad. A rent-roll analysis on a King Street building should weight trailing twelve-month revenue over any single strong season, since a peak-month figure alone can overstate what a tenant can reliably pay across a full year.

sections.heading: Procurement Watchouts Inside the Historic Boundary
sections.html:
Beyond the Certificate of Appropriateness requirement, buyers should scope any prior code-enforcement history on a historic-district building, since deferred exterior maintenance is common on older storefronts and can trigger a compliance order after closing if it went unaddressed by a prior owner. Flood zone status is also a recurring line item given the city's low elevation and bayfront proximity, and a lender's flood-insurance requirement should be confirmed early in the procurement schedule rather than assumed.

St. Johns County's permitting office operates independently of both the City of St. Augustine and Duval County, so a title review should confirm which authority actually has jurisdiction over utility connections and right-of-way work on a given parcel.

Archaeological review is a further line item unique to this submarket: ground-disturbing work on many downtown parcels can require a monitoring plan given the density of colonial-era artifacts beneath the historic core, and a buyer planning any below-grade utility or foundation work should confirm this requirement with the city's archaeology program before finalizing a construction budget.

sections.heading: Positioning St. Augustine on an Identification List
sections.html:
Given the historic district's approval timeline, a St. Augustine candidate typically works better as one line on a three-property identification list rather than the sole target under the 45-day window, with Ponte Vedra Beach or the World Golf Village corridor serving as faster-moving backups if the historic-district review runs long. Buyers who need a shorter closing timeline often shift their primary focus to the US-1 corridor outside the preservation boundary, where standard permitting applies.

A qualified intermediary coordinating a St. Augustine closing should also confirm early how the historic-district approval timeline interacts with the full 180-day exchange period rather than only the 45-day identification window, since a slow renovation permit after closing can still affect a buyer's broader financing and repositioning plan even after the exchange itself has completed.

faqs.q: Why does a historic-district building in St. Augustine take longer to close?
faqs.a: Any exterior or signage change inside the preservation boundary requires a Certificate of Appropriateness, which runs on its own review calendar separate from standard building permits, so buyers should build extra weeks into the closing schedule.

faqs.q: Is tourism demand in St. Augustine steady year-round?
faqs.a: No, it follows a seasonal pattern tied to weather and school schedules, so a rent-roll review should rely on trailing twelve-month figures rather than a single peak month when underwriting a restaurant or retail tenant.

faqs.q: Does flood zone status matter for St. Augustine commercial property?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's low elevation and bayfront proximity make flood zone confirmation and lender insurance requirements a standard line item in due diligence, not an optional check.

faqs.q: Can a buyer avoid the historic review process entirely?
faqs.a: Only by identifying property outside the preservation boundary, such as newer commercial pads along US-1 or State Road 16, which follow standard St. Johns County permitting rather than the city's historic design review.

faqs.q: What backup markets pair well with a St. Augustine identification?
faqs.a: Ponte Vedra Beach and the World Golf Village corridor are the two most common backups, since both offer faster-moving inventory if a St. Augustine historic-district approval runs past the 45-day identification window.
